title: MCA band brochures and deciding on a career in bands
summary: As a grade-school kid he collected MCA brochures of uniformed bands and decided that was what he wanted to do.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: All right, let's see. Oh, yeah. Did you
really consider this as a career-oriented thing when you were playing in the, say, high school period? Were you looking toward it as a --

Yeah, I'm afraid I must have been, because, for instance, somehow or other, through friends and people I worked with in the theatre and so on, I was able to gather a number of brochures which were put out as advertising pieces, I guess, by Music Corporation of America and other agencies, but mainly the MCA ones, I remember, because they had marvelous photographs of all these bands they handled, in full regalia and uniforms and thousands of instruments in front of each player.

And this was very, very impressive to me, and as a matter of fact, I think right then and there, that at whatever age I was, -- and it had to be still in grade school -- that was what I wanted to do. That was bigger than being a ball player or anything else.
